title: Cap. IV Arg. 1 Sol: first — largo sensu any decree can be called praedestinatio, but theology specializes
latin: Sol. Priusquam ad argumenti solutionem veniamus, quia in ipso vocabulo praedestinationis subinde nobis illudunt adversarii, de eo aliquid dicemus. Est igitur primo notandum, posse quidem sensu largo quodlibet Dei decretum de re qualibet vocari decretum praedestinationis. Ratio aperta est; quia omnia Dei decreta sunt ab aeterno in mente Divina concepta, et secundum destinatum propositum voluntatis Divinae. Verum cum usus loquendi in sacra Theologia hoc vocabulum praedestinationis ad specialem quandam significationem arctaverit, non est ingenui Theologi sub generali notione vocabuli ludum facere auditoribus.
pass_a: Solution. Before we come to the solution of the argument, because in the very word of predestination the adversaries from time to time mock us, we will say something concerning it. It is therefore first to be noted that in a broad sense any decree of God concerning any thing can indeed be called a decree of predestination. The reason is open; because all God's decrees are conceived from eternity in the Divine mind, and according to the destined purpose of the Divine will. But since the usage of speaking in sacred Theology has narrowed this word of predestination to a certain special signification, it is not of a candid Theologian to make a game for his hearers under the general notion of the word.
pass_b: Sol. Before solving the argument: adversaries keep playing with the word predestination, so a word on that. First: in a broad sense any decree of God about anything can be called a decree of predestination — all God's decrees are conceived from eternity in the divine mind according to the destined purpose of the divine will. But sacred theology has narrowed that word to a special sense; it is not candid theology to play games with hearers under the general notion.

title: Cap. IV Arg. 1 Sol: second — not every revealed placitum is the high Pauline predestination
latin: Secundo et illud perpendendum, In praesenti nostra controversia Theologos nunquam per decretum praedestinationis intellexisse quodlibet placitum Divinae voluntatis de salute et exitio hominum, sub qualibet forma conceptum et in verbo revelatum. Nam si eo hoc vocabulum torquere libeat, ipsissimum decretum praedestinationis continebitur illis verbis Matth. xxv. 34. &c. Dicet Rex iis qui sunt ad dextram, Venite benedicti Patris mei, possidete regnum paratum vobis a jactis mundi fundamentis. Esurivi enim et dedistis mihi quo vescerer, &c. Dicet iis qui ad sinistram erunt, Abite maledicti in ignem aeternum, qui paratus est diabolo et angelis ejus. Esurivi enim, et non dedistis mihi quo vescerer, &c. Exprimetur etiam praedestinationis decretum et in illis ad Rom. ii. 6. Deus reddet unicuique secundum opera ipsius: iis quidem qui perstant, boni operis gloriam et honorem et immortalitatem: iis vero qui sunt contentiosi, et qui veritati non obtemperant, sed obtemperant injustitiae, reddetur excandescentia et ira, &c. In hisce enim et similibus locis, patefit nobis voluntas Dei de salute et exitio hominum, et tamen in hujusmodi decretis ponere illam altam et inscrutabilem praedestinationem quam Paulus cantopere celebrat et admiratur, est a sensu et sententia Scripturarum, atque omnium sanorum Theologorum alienissimum.
pass_a: Second, that also is to be weighed: In our present controversy Theologians have never understood by the decree of predestination any pleasure of the Divine will whatsoever concerning the salvation and ruin of men, conceived under any form and revealed in the word. For if one is pleased to twist this word thither, the very decree of predestination itself will be contained in those words of Matt. 25:34 etc. The King will say to those who are on the right, Come, blessed of my Father, possess the kingdom prepared for you from the foundations of the world laid. For I hungered and you gave me what to eat, etc. He will say to those who will be on the left, Depart, cursed, into eternal fire, which is prepared for the devil and his angels. For I hungered, and you did not give me what to eat, etc. The decree of predestination will also be expressed in those at Rom. 2:6. God will render to each according to his works: to those indeed who persist, glory and honor and immortality of good work: but to those who are contentious, and who do not obey the truth, but obey injustice, heat and wrath will be rendered, etc. For in these and similar places the will of God concerning the salvation and ruin of men is opened to us, and yet to place in such decrees that high and inscrutable predestination which Paul so greatly celebrates and admires is most alien from the sense and sentence of the Scriptures, and of all sound Theologians.
pass_b: Second: in our controversy theologians have never meant by the predestination decree any revealed pleasure of the divine will about men's salvation and ruin, under any form. Twist the word that way and Matt. 25:34ff. itself becomes the decree — Come, blessed of my Father… Depart, cursed… — and so does Rom. 2:6, God will render to each according to his works. Those places do open God's will about salvation and ruin; but to lodge in them that high, inscrutable predestination Paul so celebrates is most alien to Scripture and to all sound theologians.

title: Cap. IV Arg. 1 Sol: third — properly a practical decree gifting singular persons grace and glory
latin: Tertio cognoscere oportet, praedestinationis decretum proprie sumptum denotare, non legem universalem ostendentem omnibus ex aequo, quo modo, vel quibus mediis, salus obtineatur, aut mors incurratur: Qualia sunt illa, Quisquis crediderit, quisquis in pietate perseveraverit, salvus erit; et contra, Quisquis non crediderit, quisquis opera pietatis non exercuerit, damnabitur. Sed praedestinatio designat practicum Dei decretum, quo ab aeterno statuit singulares quasdam personas singularibus bonis, hoc est, gratia efficaci et vita aeterna, infallibiliter donare. Sic Paulus praedestinationem accipit Rom. viii; quando illam ad quasdam certas personas restringit, et cum glorificatione inseparabili nexu conjungit: sic Schola Theologorum, quae illam definivit Praeparationem gratiae in praesenti, et gloriae in futuro. Decreta ergo illa in quibus exponitur tantum generatim qualibus hominibus vita aeterna donabitur, qualibus mors aeterna infligetur, interim autem nihil statuitur de danda gratia et gloria ullis singularibus personis; talia, inquam, decreta vim naturamque praedestinationis non exprimunt.
pass_a: Third it is necessary to know that the decree of predestination properly taken denotes, not a universal law showing to all equally by what manner, or by what means, salvation is obtained, or death is incurred: Such as are those, Whoever will have believed, whoever will have persevered in piety, will be saved; and on the contrary, Whoever will not have believed, whoever will not have exercised works of piety, will be damned. But predestination designates a practical decree of God, by which from eternity he established to gift certain singular persons infallibly with singular goods, that is, with efficacious grace and eternal life. So Paul takes predestination in Rom. 8; when he restricts it to certain definite persons, and joins it with glorification by an inseparable bond: so the School of Theologians, which defined it Preparation of grace in the present, and of glory in the future. Those decrees therefore in which it is set forth only generally to what sort of men eternal life will be gifted, to what sort eternal death will be inflicted, while meanwhile nothing is established concerning grace and glory to be given to any singular persons; such decrees, I say, do not express the force and nature of predestination.
pass_b: Third: predestination properly taken does not mean a universal law showing all alike how salvation is obtained or death incurred — Whoever believes and perseveres in piety will be saved; whoever does not believe or practice piety will be damned. It designates a practical decree by which from eternity God established to gift certain singular persons infallibly with singular goods: efficacious grace and eternal life. So Paul takes it in Rom. 8, restricting it to definite persons and joining it inseparably with glorification; so the School, which defined it Preparation of grace in the present and of glory in the future. Decrees that only say generally what sort of men get eternal life or death, while settling nothing about grace and glory for any singular persons, do not express predestination's force and nature.

title: Cap. IV Arg. 1 Sol: Major — if universal, false; revealed qualities/acts ≠ formal decree
latin: Hisce praemissis accedo ad rationem propositam, ac dico Majorem, cujus illi veritatem manifestam esse clamant, aut manifeste falsam esse, aut particularem, atque tum ex omnibus particularibus inepta erit conclusio. Si Major universalis sit, hoc modo, Quaelibet Dei voluntas de salute et exitio hominum in Evangelio patefacta, est totum et integrum decretum praedestinationis, manifeste falsa est. Deus enim revelavit voluntatem suam quoad qualitates quibus praediti debent esse omnes qui futuri sunt aeternae vitae participes; revelavit voluntatem suam quoad actus, qui exerceri debent ab omnibus, qui ingredi volunt vitam aeternam; hisce tamen quasi statutis humano generi revelatis, non continetur formale decretum praedestinationis Divinae; sed in illa arcana intentione sive voluntate efficaciter et infallibiliter donandi electis quibusdam illas qualitates, eos actus, qui ducunt ad vitam aeternam, ipsamque vitam aeternam.
pass_a: These things having been premised I come to the reason proposed, and I say that the Major, whose truth they cry out to be manifest, is either manifestly false, or particular, and then from all particulars the conclusion will be inept. If the Major be universal, in this manner, Any will of God whatsoever concerning the salvation and ruin of men revealed in the Gospel is the whole and entire decree of predestination, it is manifestly false. For God has revealed his will as to the qualities with which all who will be partakers of eternal life ought to be endowed; he has revealed his will as to the acts which ought to be exercised by all who will to enter eternal life; yet in these as it were statutes revealed to the human race the formal decree of the Divine predestination is not contained; but in that secret intention or will of efficaciously and infallibly gifting to certain elect those qualities, those acts, which lead to eternal life, and eternal life itself.
pass_b: With that premised I turn to their reason. The Major they call self-evident is either manifestly false, or particular — and then from particulars the conclusion is inept. If universal — Any gospel-revealed will of God about men's salvation and ruin is the whole entire decree of predestination — it is manifestly false. God has revealed his will about the qualities all who will share eternal life must have, and about the acts all who will enter that life must exercise; yet those revealed statutes do not contain the formal decree of divine predestination. That lies in the secret intention or will to gift certain elect efficaciously and infallibly those qualities and acts that lead to eternal life, and eternal life itself.

title: Cap. IV Arg. 1 Sol: whole saving will includes vocation according to purpose — true praedestinans will
latin: Tota siquidem Dei voluntas de salute hominum non continetur tali decreto, Qui crediderit habebit vitam aeternam. Nam in sacris Scripturis Deus insuper patefecit, se quibusdam, quorum ex mero beneplacito vult prae aliis misereri, velle donare vocationem secundum propositum; ex tali vocatione poenitentiam, fidem, sanctificationem, et demum glorificationem, atque haec omnia infallibiliter. Haec voluntas Dei est vera et proprie voluntas praedestinans, estque in Evangelio patefacta quoad rem, quamvis individua quoad nomen non inibi exprimantur. Haec de Majore.
pass_a: For the whole will of God concerning the salvation of men is not contained in such a decree, Whoever will have believed will have eternal life. For in the sacred Scriptures God has moreover opened that he wills to gift to certain ones, of whom from mere good pleasure he wills to have mercy before others, a vocation according to purpose; from such vocation repentance, faith, sanctification, and finally glorification, and all these things infallibly. This will of God is the true and properly predestinating will, and is opened in the Gospel as to the thing, although the individuals as to name are not there expressed. These things concerning the Major.
pass_b: For God's whole will about men's salvation is not contained in Whoever believes will have eternal life. Scripture further opens that to certain ones — of whom from mere good pleasure he wills to have mercy before others — he wills to gift vocation according to purpose; from that vocation repentance, faith, sanctification, and finally glorification, all infallibly. That is the true, properly predestinating will, opened in the Gospel as to the thing, though individuals are not there named. So much for the Major.

title: Cap. IV Arg. 1 Sol close: Minor true — inference that this is whole predestination weakest
latin: De Minore, quae fundatur in expressis quibusdam Scripturae locis, sufficiat hoc unum dixisse, Verissimum esse quod assumitur, Deum patefecisse in Evangelio hanc suam voluntatem servandi illos omnes qui in fide perseverabunt, et damnandi incredulos; sed infirmissimum esse quod inde inferre volunt, In hoc decreto voluntatis Divinae positam esse praedestinationem hominum, imo totum et integrum decretum praedestinationis nostrae. Verum cum ad nostra argumenta ventum fuerit, hoc insomnia Arminianum dispellemus.
pass_a: Concerning the Minor, which is founded in certain express places of Scripture, let it suffice to have said this one thing, That what is assumed is most true, that God has opened in the Gospel this his will of saving all those who will persevere in faith, and of damning unbelievers; but that what they will to infer thence is most weak, That in this decree of the Divine will the predestination of men is placed, nay the whole and entire decree of our predestination. But when it will have come to our arguments, we will dispel this Arminian dream.
pass_b: On the Minor, founded in certain express Scripture places, one thing suffices: what they assume is most true — God has opened in the Gospel his will to save all who will persevere in faith and to damn unbelievers. What they infer from it is weakest: that in this decree of the divine will men's predestination is placed — nay the whole and entire decree of our predestination. When we come to our own arguments, we will dispel this Arminian dream.
